::: {#exm-covariate-patterns}

#### Covariate patterns in the low-birth-weight data

The `birthwt` data record whether each of `r nrow(read.csv("data/birthwt.csv"))` babies had low birth weight
(`low = 1`, under 2.5 kg), along with the mother's smoking status and race, among other predictors
[@hosmer1989applied].
Take `smoke` (0 or 1) and `race` (1, 2 or 3) as the predictors.
Counting the distinct pairs, and the babies and low-weight births at each, gives one row per [covariate pattern](#def-covariate-pattern).

```{r}
#| code-fold: false
bw <- read.csv("data/birthwt.csv")
bw$race <- factor(bw$race)
# one row per covariate pattern: replicates and events
bw_grouped <- bw |>
  dplyr::summarize(
    nreps = dplyr::n(),
    nevents = sum(low),
    .by = c(smoke, race)
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(smoke, race)
bw_grouped
```

There are $\npatterns = `r nrow(bw_grouped)`$ covariate patterns among $\nobs = `r nrow(bw)`$ babies.
The pattern with the most [replicates](#def-replicates) has `smoke` = `r bw_grouped$smoke[which.max(bw_grouped$nreps)]` and
`race` = `r bw_grouped$race[which.max(bw_grouped$nreps)]`, and it has `r max(bw_grouped$nreps)` of them.

:::
